### 📜 Poem – 1     ONCE UPON A TIME


> **i.  Once upon a time, son  They used to laugh with their hearts**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are taken from the poem “Once upon a Time” written by Gabriel Okara, a Nigerian poet.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *The poem is a father’s address to his son., where the father wants to learn from his son how to go back to normality and no longer fake. The poem starts by the father telling his son how the people used to laugh with their hearts in olden times.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *This description in the poem gives the impression of genuine emotion given off by the people in the past*

> **ii. There will be no thrice**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are taken from the poem “Once upon a Time” written by Gabriel Okara, a Nigerian poet.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *In the first line of the third stanza “Feel at home!”, “Come again” the poet uses fake cordiality.  People welcome the guests for two times but the third time they will treat differently.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *Their falseness is reflected in the language they use.*

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are taken from the poem “Once upon a Time” written by Gabriel Okara, a Nigerian poet.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *The poet presents the adaptations and solutions that the man has found to counter the problems. He tells of the false personalities or of his ‘many faces’. He says that he has an ‘office-face, street-face, and host-face, proving that he acts differently under different circumstances. He then adds that they have, ‘conforming smiles, like a fixed portrait’.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *This suggests, even more, falseness and changes.*

> **iv. I want to be what I used to be**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are taken from the poem “Once upon a Time” written by Gabriel Okara, a Nigerian poet.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *The poet tells his son that he wants to go back to his childhood. He wants to get back his lost identity. He expresses a desire to unlearn whatever he has forced himself to learn.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *He asks his son to help him be happy once again and acquire the childlike innocence he once possessed as a child.*

### 📜 Poem – 2    CONFESSIONS OF A BORN SPECTATOR


> **i. I am just glad as glad can  be That I am not them, that they are not me..**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are taken from the poem “Confessions of a born spectator” written by Ogden Nash Explanation : In this poem the poet wants to be a mere spectator of sports. His own spirit is weak and shy. So he confesses that he is glad that he is neither a sportsman nor an athlete. He always wants to be a spectator but not a participant.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *The poet is very firm in his stand.*

> **ii. They do not ever in their dealings Consider one another’s feelings**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are from the poem “Confessions of a born spectator” written by Ogden Nash.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *The poet is a determined spectator. He knows that the athletes play rough.  They do not care for their opponents.  They are self-centered and over enthusiastic and so they are indifferent to the feelings of others.  Even the umpires and referees are not moved by the injury suffered by the athletes.  The spectator finds himself unfit for such roughness and callousness.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *Though the poet is emotionally disturbed, he takes a firm decision of not taking part in any sports activities.*

> **iii. Athletes, I’ll drink to you,    Or eat with you,Or anything except compete with you…………..**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above lines are from the poem “Confessions of a born spectator” written by Ogden Nash.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *Addressing athletes, he says that he will gladly drink to their health and also dine with them, but he will never compete with them in  the playground.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *The poet is a determined spectator. He does not want to take any risk by becoming a sportsman.*

### 📜 Poem – 3  Lines Written in Early Spring


> **i) In that sweet mood when pleasant thoughtsBring sad thoughts to the mind.**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The given lines are from the poem  “Lines written in Early Spring” written by William Wordsworth.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *The poet sits reclined in a beautiful grove, surrounded by the mixed sounds of nature. He thinks of the sad thoughts brought along with the pleasant memories.*

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The given lines are from the poem “Lines written in Early Spring” written by William Wordsworth.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *The poet describes the joy of birds here.  They sang, hopped and played around the poet.  Though the poet doesn’t understand the language and ways of the birds, he recognizes their movements are out of sheer pleasure and joy.*

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The given lines are from the poem  “Lines written in Early Spring” written by “William Wordsworth”.*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *These are the concluding lines of the poem.  Nature is full of beauties and sweetness and calmness.  But men do not enjoy the beauty, but destroy nature. Men also fight against one another and all become unhappy.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *The poet becomes sad to think of what man has made of man.*

> **iv. There may be a scrap of paper in the hall or on the stair**

**A:** *The above lines are from the poem “Macavity - The Mystery Cat” written by T.S.Eliot. Explanation :  Macavity takes away some Treaty or some plans and drawings from the Admiralty. The police may find a piece of paper in the hall, but that will not help the police macavity leaves no clue or evidence.*

### 📜 Poem – 6     THE HOLLOW CROWN


> **i. ழுரச டயனௌஇ ழரச டiஎநள் and யடடஇ யசந டீழடiபெடிசழமந’ளஇ And ழெவாiபெ உயn றந உயடட ழரசஇ ழறn டிரவ னநயவர் ஊழவெநஒவ :  வுhந யடிழஎந பiஎநn டiநௌ யசந வயமநn கசழஅ றுடைடயைஅ ளூயமநளிநயசந’ள pடயல மiபெ சுiஉhயசன ஐஐ. வுhந pயளளயபந ளை யெஅநன “ர்ழடடழற ஊசழறn”**
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *King Richard II was defeated by his cousin Bolingbroke.  Therefore Richard says that his lands and all properties are taken by Bolingbroke.  Now nothing is his, except his own death.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *This passage shows the desperate, hopeless state of mind of king Richard.*

> **ii. “All murdered - for within the hollow crown That rounds the mortal temples of a king keeps Death his court,…. Context : The above given lines are taken from William Shakespeare’s play king Richard II. The passage is named “Hollow Crown”**
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *King Richard II thinks of all the kings who have been murdered by the deposer or poisoned by their wives or killed in war.  Now he realizes that within the hollow crown that sits on the kings head, Death keeps his court (his followers and agents).*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *This passage shows the understanding of King Richard on the crown.*

> **iii. “Comes at the last, and with a little pin  Bores through his castle wall, and farewell king!” Context :  The above given lines are taken from William Shakespeare’s play King Richard II.  The passage is named “Hollow Crown”**
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *Death sits within the hollow crown of the king.  It allows a short time to monarchise and show his power and authority.  But at the end, Death bores the head of the king with a pin and the king’s life is over.  There is death.*
**Q:** Comment
**A:** *Here Shakespeare uses imagery.  The king’s head is imagined to be a castle wall. Death pricks the wall and the king dies – Farewell king.*

> **iv. “How can you say to me, I am a king?”**

**Q:** Context
**A:** *The above given lines are taken from William Shakespeare’s play king Richard II. The passage is named “Hollow Crown”*
**Q:** Explanation
**A:** *King Richard is in a desperate mood.  Now he realises that he is also a human like all others.  He lives by bread.  He has his own needs and desires.  He wants to have friends.  He experiences happiness and unhappiness like all other men. Therefore he asks his followers “Why do you call me king?”. I am a human being like you.*
